data.headline: Flood Watch issued November 25 at 4:58AM EST until November 26 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Miami FL
data.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal
Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County
and Metropolitan Miami Dade.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The last 30 days of rainfall has been 400 to 600 percent of
normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and
between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of
Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground
very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida,
and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated
flooding issues across the east coast metro areas.

Most likely amounts: 2-4 inches of rain.

Reasonable Worst Case (High-End): 5-7 inches of rain. A few
locations could see 10 or more inches of rain.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
data.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

data.headline: Coastal Flood Statement issued November 24 at 11:20PM EST until November 26 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Miami FL
data.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Statement, isolated minor coastal
flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Statement, through Thursday
morning. For the High Rip Current Risk, from 4 AM EST
Wednesday through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Some water on low lying roads and property. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
data.instruction:
Do not drive through flooded roadways.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

data.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 25 at 8:34AM EST until November 25 at 9:00AM EST by NWS Miami FL
data.description:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM...
Waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM
excluding the territorial waters of Bahamas...
Waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 900 AM EST.

* At 834 AM EST, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from 28 nm
southeast of Pacific Reef to 30 nm east of Floyd's Wall Northeast,
moving north at 25 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas.

* Severe thunderstorms will remain over mainly open waters.
data.instruction:
Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.

AFDMFL

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Miami FL
656 AM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 655 AM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

  - Periods of heavy rain today which may lead to flooding
    especially over SE FL. 

  - Severe storms possible today with the primary threats being
    damaging wind gusts and a few tornadoes. 

  - Minor to moderate coastal flooding around high tide today.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Thursday)
Issued at 207 AM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

Early signs of the developing system have started to appear over 
South Florida. The forerunning shortwave has encroached South 
Florida overnight and opened up the first round of showers in 
northern Miami-Dade. Out over the gulf, the latest Weather 
Prediction Center (WPC) surface analysis shows a broad area of low
pressure expanding north east along the stationary frontal 
boundary. This area is expected to continue to deepen under the 
intensifying short-wave embedded trough moving out over the gulf 
over the course of today. A the anticipated low pressure center is
expected to form near the northwest tip of Cuba by morning before
making a slow march north east towards South Florida. 

Ensemble guidance, the European and Canadian global along with the 
REFS high-resolution, is beginning to converge on a preferred track 
of the low pressure that takes it over South Florida by mid 
afternoon today. A notable outlier is the American ensemble which
still prefers a faster moving low pressure track. There is still 
some variance in the track within the slower moving solutions with
60% taking the low over Southeast Florida while 40% take the low 
center over Central Florida. 

Both scenarios favor thunderstorm development through the morning 
today and an increasing severe potential for the afternoon. The 
latest outlook from the Storm Prediction Center agrees with this and 
has bumped Southeast Florida up from a 'Marginal' to 'Slight' severe 
threat. SPC has also increased the tornado probability to 5% over 
Southeast Florida, specifically over Miami-Dade and Broward counties 
with a 2% risk for the remainder of Southeast Florida. Uncertainty 
this afternoon still revolves around the orientation and strength of 
the 850mb jet in conjunction with how high the afternoon CAPE values 
climb to while under the warm sector of the approaching low.The 
upper end of rainfall value ranges for today have steadily climbed 
with each update from ensemble guidance. Wide spread 2-4 inches for 
all of South Florida with localized areas seeing up to 5-7 inches 
and 10+ possible as a worst case scenario. 

Moving into Thursday, rainfall will tail off Wednesday night into 
early Thursday morning and should be completely out of the area by 
Thursday afternoon. High temps for Thursday will be in the mid to 
high 70s with the lows creeping down to the high 60s as a cool and 
dy airmass moves over South Florida.

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Thursday night through Tuesday)
Issued at 207 AM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

High pressure and zonal flow aloft will result in dry and cooler 
than normal conditions for Friday and Saturday. Attention then turns 
to an upper level low cutting across Mexico which will get absorbed 
into the larger longwave trough late in the weekend. This trough 
will swing through the eastern US late in the weekend into early 
next week. Moisture will increase ahead of an approaching front 
bringing the threat for showers back into the forecast for late 
Sunday into early next week. Temperatures will also be on the 
increase back to around seasonal norms by early next week.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 655 AM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

Widespread rain, locally heavy at times, will impact the terminals
today. Prevailing MVFR ceilings expected with some periods of
IFR/LIFR during heavy rainfall. Easterly winds around 10 kts,
however occasional thunderstorms may result in gusty, erratic 
winds.

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 207 AM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

Hazardous winds and seas for both the Atlantic and Gulf waters 
through at least Thursday evening. Southerly winds 20-30 kts today 
becoming westerly on Thursday. Seas building to 4-8 ft. 
Thunderstorms are expected throughout the day today. 

&&

.BEACHES...
Issued at 207 AM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

Due to the king tides and heavy rainfall, moderate coastal flooding 
is possible today around high tide for Palm Beach and Broward, with 
minor coastal flooding for the rest of the area coastline. Minor 
coastal flooding is expected on Thursday before conditions improve 
on Friday. 

Increasing swell will result in a high risk of rip currents for the 
Atlantic beaches beginning today, and Collier county beaches on 
Thursday.

&&

&&

.MFL WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
FL...Flood Watch through late tonight for FLZ068-072-074-168-172-173.

     High Rip Current Risk from late tonight through Thursday evening 
     for FLZ069.
